author: Philippe Vieu
text: In bivariate density representation there is an extensive literature on level set estimation when the level is fixed but this is not so much the case when choosing which level is or which levels are of most interest This is an important practical question which depends on the kind of problem one has to deal with as well as the kind of feature one wishes to highlight in the density the answer to which requires both the definition of what the optimal level is and the construction of a method for finding it We consider two scenarios for this problem The first one corresponds to situations in which one has just a single density function to be represented However as a result of the technical progress in data collecting problems are emerging in which one has to deal with a sample of densities In these situations the need arises to develop joint representation for all these densities and this is the second scenario considered in this paper For each case we provide consistency results for the estimated levels and present wide Monte Carlo simulated experiments illustrating the interest and feasibility of the proposed method C Elsevier Inc

author: Philippe Vieu
text: The aim of this article is to study the knearest neighbour kNN method in nonparametric functional regression We present asymptotic properties of the kNN kernel estimator the almostcomplete convergence and its rate Then we illustrate the effectiveness of this method by comparing it with the traditional kernel approach first on simulated datasets and then on a real chemometrical example We also present in this article an important technical tool which could be useful in many other situations than ours

author: Philippe Vieu
text: We consider the problem of predicting a real random variable from a functional explanatory variable The problem is tackled using a nonparametric kernel approach which has been recently adapted to this functional context We derive theoretical results from a deep asymptotic analysis of the behaviour of the estimate including mean squared convergence with rates and precise evaluation of the constant terms as well as asymptotic distribution Practical use of these results relies on the ability to estimate these constants Some perspectives in this direction are discussed In particular a functional version of wild bootstrapping ideas is proposed and used both on simulated and real functional datasets

author: Philippe Vieu
text: We consider a nonparametric regression model where the response Y and the covariate X are both functional ie valued in some infinitedimensional space We define a kernel type estimator of the regression operator and we first establish its pointwise asymptotic normality The double functional feature of the problem makes the formulas of the asymptotic bias and variance even harder to estimate than in more standard regression settings and we propose to overcome this difficulty by using resampling ideas Both a naive and a wild componentwise bootstrap procedure are studied and their asymptotic validity is proved These results are also extended to datadriven bases which is a key point for implementing this methodology The theoretical advances are completed by some simulation studies showing both the practical feasibility of the method and the good behavior for finite sample sizes of the kernel estimator and of the bootstrap procedures to build functional pseudoconfidence area C Elsevier Inc All rights

author: Philippe Vieu
text: In this paper we consider the functional linear model with scalar response and explanatory variable valued in a function space In recent literature functional principal components analysis FPCA has been used to estimate the model parameter We propose to modify this approach by using presmoothing techniques For this new estimate consistency is stated and efficiency by comparison with the standard FPCA estimator is studied We have also analysed the behaviour of our presmoothed estimator by means of a simulation study and data applications

author: Philippe Vieu
text: This paper focuses on partially linear regression models with several real and functional covariates The aim is to construct an estimate of the variance of the error In our model a realvalued response variable is explained by the sum of an unknown linear combination of the components of a multivariate random variable and an unknown transformation of a functional random variable and the second sample moment based on residuals from a semiparametric fit is proposed for estimating the error variance Then the asymptotic normality and the law of the iterated logarithm of such estimator are obtained Finally a simulation study illustrates the finite sample behaviour of the estimator while an application to real data shows the usefulness of the proposed methodology more specifically for confidence region construction

author: Philippe Vieu
text: This note deals with the problem of predicting some realvalued response variable in the situation where some among the explanatory variables are functional More precisely a new model is introduced in order to capture both the advantages of a semilinear modelling and those of the recent advances on nonparametric statistics for functional data The aim of this note is to provide the first advances in this direction After having constructed precisely the socalled semifunctional partially linear model the estimates are presented and some asymptotic results with rates of convergence are given Lastly a real data example illustrates the usefulness of the model C Published by Elsevier BV

author: Philippe Vieu
text: A topological hypothesis was omitted during the statement of the results in This erratum states this additional hypothesis It also provides a wide class of examples of functional spaces of statistical interest for which this new hypothesis is satisfied

author: Philippe Vieu
text: This paper addresses the challenge of optimal representation of bivariate probability densities through level sets a crucial aspect in statistical analysis and data visualization We introduce a systematic approach to determine optimal level sets that minimize the discrepancy between the true density function and its estimated representation while ensuring computational efficiency By leveraging techniques from multivariate analysis and information theory we develop a framework that identifies the most informative contours of the bivariate distribution Our proposed method integrates both analytical and numerical strategies providing a robust procedure for constructing level sets that enhance interpretability and facilitate statistical inference We showcase the effectiveness of our approach through simulation studies and realworld applications demonstrating significant improvements in representation quality compared to traditional methods The implications of our findings extend to various fields including machine learning spatial statistics and econometrics where understanding complex relationships within bivariate data is essential

author: Philippe Vieu
text: This paper investigates the application of the Knearest neighbour KNN method within the framework of functional nonparametric regression We propose a novel approach that leverages the KNN algorithm to effectively model complex functional relationships enabling the estimation of regression functions without assuming a specific parametric form Our methodology is built upon a solid theoretical foundation specifically addressing the challenges posed by highdimensional functional data including issues related to curse of dimensionality and distance metrics We provide a comprehensive analysis of the KNN methods performance against established nonparametric techniques employing asymptotic properties and bounding convergence rates to demonstrate its efficacy in capturing local structure in functional data Simulation studies are conducted to validate our theoretical findings showcasing the KNN methods robustness and adaptability across various functional forms Furthermore we present an application to realworld data highlighting the practical implications of our approach in enhancing predictive accuracy for functional regression problems The results underscore the potential of KNN as a powerful tool in the realm of functional nonparametric regression paving the way for further research in this promising area

author: Philippe Vieu
text: In this paper we explore nonparametric regression techniques applied to functional data focusing on both statistical inference and practical implementation Functional data which encompasses observations that are curves images or other infinitedimensional objects presents unique challenges for traditional regression methodologies We propose a comprehensive framework that integrates multiple nonparametric approaches to regression analysis including kernel smoothing and spline methods tailored for the complexities of functional data structures We establish the theoretical underpinnings of our techniques demonstrating convergence rates and asymptotic properties under various conditions Through extensive simulations we assess the finitesample performance of our methods identifying scenarios where nonparametric approaches outperform parametric counterparts We further discuss practical considerations such as bandwidth selection and computational efficiency providing a userfriendly guide for practitioners in various fields including biostatistics econometrics and environmental sciences Our results underscore the versatility and robustness of nonparametric regression in handling diverse types of functional data paving the way for more accurate modeling and inference in realworld applications We conclude with case studies that illustrate the practical utility of our methodologies highlighting their implications for future research and exploratory data analysis in functional contexts

author: Philippe Vieu
text: AbstractIn this paper we explore a novel approach to regression analysis where both the response variable and predictors are treated as functions rather than traditional scalar values This functional regression framework allows for capturing complex relationships that may be missed in classical approaches particularly in scenarios involving longitudinal data curves or spatial processes We develop a comprehensive theoretical foundation for functional regression including estimation methods hypothesis testing and model selection criteria Furthermore we present a simulation study to illustrate the effectiveness of our proposed methods comparing them with standard regression techniques We apply our approach to realworld datasets from various fields demonstrating its capability to uncover intricate functional dependencies Finally we discuss potential extensions of our methods and their implications for advancing functional data analysis Our findings highlight the importance of considering a functional perspective in regression settings paving the way for more robust and insightful statistical modeling

author: Philippe Vieu
text: AbstractIn this paper we investigate the concept of presmoothing within the framework of functional linear regression FLR where the response variable is scalar and the predictor is a function Traditional FLR methods often face challenges due to noise in the functional data which can adversely affect estimation and inference To address these challenges we propose a presmoothing technique that preemptively mitigates noise in the functional predictor prior to the application of FLR Our methodology involves the use of local polynomial smoothing and other modern smoothing techniques to enhance the underlying functional signals We rigorously demonstrate that presmoothing can lead to improved estimator properties including consistency bias reduction and increased efficiency We provide theoretical results that establish the asymptotic behavior of the proposed estimator as well as highdimensional consistency results under specific conditions Additionally we conduct a series of simulations to illustrate the practical effectiveness of our approach compared to traditional methods without presmoothing Application to realworld datasets further highlights the advantages of presmoothing in functional linear regression settings Our findings suggest that presmoothing is a valuable preprocessing step that can greatly enhance the statistical performance of FLR modelsKeywords Functional linear regression presmoothing local polynomial smoothing estimator efficiency asymptotic behavior

author: Philippe Vieu
text: This paper addresses the challenge of error variance estimation in semifunctional partially linear regression models which are increasingly utilized in econometrics and social sciences for their ability to model complex relationships involving both functional and nonfunctional predictors We develop a novel estimation technique that combines robust statistical methods and asymptotic theory to provide accurate estimates of error variance in these models Our method accounts for the inherent structure of functional data while managing the nonparametric components effectively Through extensive simulation studies we demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of bias variance and overall mean squared error especially under varying degrees of functional complexity and sample sizes Additionally we apply our proposed method to a realworld dataset illustrating its practical applicability and the importance of accurate error variance estimation in enhancing model interpretation and inference The findings contribute valuable insights toward improving the reliability of statistical inference in semifunctional partially linear regression frameworks paving the way for future research in this area

author: Philippe Vieu
text: This paper introduces a novel statistical methodology termed Semifunctional Partial Linear Regression SFPLR which efficiently models the relationship between a scalar response variable and a combination of functional predictors and traditional multivariate covariates In many applied settings data may consist of both highdimensional functional data eg time series curves and standard quantitative variables posing challenges for conventional regression techniques Our proposed SFPLR framework extends the classical partial linear regression approach by integrating functional data analysis allowing for the estimation of nonlinear relationships while retaining the flexibility of linear components associated with covariates We derive the estimation procedure based on a twostep approach involving functional principal component analysis and penalized least squares estimation to capture the intricate structures within the functional data Theoretical properties including consistency and asymptotic normality of the estimators are established under mild conditions We also conduct extensive simulation studies to illustrate the performance of the SFPLR method in various scenarios in comparison to existing flexible regression techniques Finally we apply SFPLR to realworld datasets demonstrating its utility in uncovering insights into complex data relationships where traditional methods may fall short Our findings indicate that SFPLR is a robust and efficient tool for addressing the challenges posed by semifunctional data making significant contributions to both statistical theory and applied research

author: Philippe Vieu
text: This erratum addresses corrections and clarifications to the original paper titled Nonparametric Models for Functional Data with Application in Regression Timeseries Prediction and Curve Discrimination In the original publication certain methodological approaches and statistical results were inadvertently misrepresented leading to potential ambiguities in interpretation Specifically we rectify errors in the formulation of the nonparametric estimators employed provide additional context for the assumptions underlying the model and elucidate the implications of these corrections on the results presented regarding regression analysis and timeseries predictions Furthermore we clarify the procedures for curve discrimination and enhance the discussion surrounding the robustness of these nonparametric methods The amendments made in this erratum are crucial for ensuring the integrity of the findings and for guiding future research in the area of functional data analysis We apologize for any confusion caused and appreciate the understanding of our readers as we strive to uphold the highest standards in statistical discourse

author: Philippe Vieu
text: There is a recent interest in developing new statistical methods to predict time series by taking into account a continuous set of past values as predictors In this functional time series prediction approach we propose a functional version of the partial linear model that allows both to consider additional covariates and to use a continuous path in the past to predict future values of the process The aim of this paper is to present this model to construct some estimates and to look at their properties both from a theoretical point of view by means of asymptotic results and from a practical perspective by treating some real data sets Although the literature on the use of parametric or nonparametric functional modeling is growing as far as we know this is the first paper on semiparametric functional modeling for the prediction of time series c Elsevier Inc

author: Philippe Vieu
text: We consider kernel regression estimate when both the response variable and the explanatory one are functional The rates of uniform almost complete convergence are stated as function of the small ball probability of the predictor and as function of the entropy of the set on which uniformity is obtained

author: Philippe Vieu
text: We investigate nonparametric curve estimation including density distribution hazard conditional density and regression functions estimation by kernel methods when the observed data satisfy a strong mixing condition In a first attempt we show asymptotic equivalence of average square errors integrated square errors and mean integrated square errors These results are extensions to dependent data of several works in particular of those by Marron and H rdle J Multivariate Anal Then we give precise asymptotic evaluations of these errors

author: Philippe Vieu
text: In this paper we investigate the asymptotic properties of the estimator for the regression function operator whenever the functional stationary ergodic data with missing at random MAR are considered Concretely we construct the kernel type estimator of the regression operator for functional stationary ergodic data with the responses MAR and some asymptotic properties such as the convergence rate in probability as well as the asymptotic normality of the estimator are obtained under some mild conditions respectively As an application the asymptotic zeta confidence interval of the regression operator is also presented for zeta Finally a simulation study is carried out to compare the finite sample performance based on mean square error between the classical functional regression in complete case and the functional regression with MAR C Elsevier BV

author: Philippe Vieu
text: A density function is generally not well defined in functional data context but we can define a surrogate of a probability density also called pseudodensity when the small ball probability can be approximated by the product of two independent functions one depending only on the centre of the ball The aim of this paper is to study two kernel methods for estimating a surrogate probability density for functional data We present asymptotic properties of these estimators the convergence in probability and their rates Simulations are given including a functional version of smoother bootstrap selection of the parameters of the estimate

author: Philippe Vieu
text: We discuss estimation and testing of hypotheses in a partial linear regression model that is a regression model where the regression function is the sum of a linear and a nonparametric component We focus on the case where the covariables and the random noise do not necessarily have summable autocovariance functions and the estimators and test statistics are based on kernel smoothing We obtain the bias variance and asymptotic distribution of both estimators for the parametric and nonparametric parts as well as the asymptotic distributions of the statistics used both under the null hypothesis and local alternatives We thus generalize the results of Speckman and of Beran and Ghosh to the case of general structures for the autocovariance function and complete the results of GonzalezManteiga and VilarFemandez to the case of a partial linear regression model Simulations and a real data example provide promising results for our tests

author: Philippe Vieu
text: In this paper we propose a novel approach to nonparametric time series prediction by introducing a Semifunctional Partial Linear Modeling framework Traditional time series prediction methods often rely on parametric assumptions that may not hold in practice leading to suboptimal forecasts Our method integrates both functional and nonfunctional components allowing for greater flexibility in capturing complex temporal patterns By leveraging nonparametric techniques we model the dynamic relationships between a response variable and a set of predictors while accommodating potential nonlinear dependencies associated with time We demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach through simulated data and realworld time series applications illustrating improvements in predictive accuracy compared to standard methods The proposed Semifunctional Partial Linear Model not only enhances the interpretability of the relationships but also offers a robust alternative for practitioners dealing with highdimensional time series data Our findings underscore the importance of nonparametric techniques in advancing the field of time series prediction setting the stage for future research in predictive modeling frameworks

author: Philippe Vieu
text: In this paper we explore kernel regression techniques tailored for functional responses expanding traditional regression methodologies to accommodate scenarios where the dependent variable manifests as a function rather than a scalar The proposed approach leverages kernel smoothing to estimate the relationship between a multivariate covariate and a functional response facilitating more nuanced modeling of data in areas such as finance medicine and environmental science where responses are often curves or surfaces We introduce a novel kernelbased estimator for functional regression establish its theoretical properties and demonstrate its consistency and asymptotic normality under weak dependence assumptions Empirical performance is evaluated through simulations and case studies illustrating the methods robustness in capturing complex relationships compared to existing approaches The findings indicate that our functional kernel regression framework provides a powerful tool for analyzing the intricacies inherent in functional data opening avenues for future research in both methodology and application

author: Philippe Vieu
text: In this paper we investigate the behavior of quadratic error metrics for nonparametric estimators in the presence of dependent data structures While classical nonparametric estimation techniques such as kernel and spline methods rely on the assumption of independent and identically distributed iid samples realworld applications often involve dependencies that can significantly affect estimation accuracy We first establish a theoretical framework that extends traditional quadratic error analysis to settings where dependence is prevalent employing mixing conditions and dependence metrics to characterize the underlying data structures Utilizing this framework we derive asymptotic results for the quadratic loss of commonly used nonparametric estimators such as kernel density estimators and local polynomial regressions highlighting the effects of dependence on convergence rates and biasvariance tradeoffs Through simulations and realdata applications we demonstrate the practical implications of our findings showing how conventional estimators can lead to misleading conclusions when dependency is ignored Our results provide a robust statistical foundation for practitioners seeking to implement nonparametric techniques in dependent contexts and we conclude with recommendations for future research to enhance the reliability of nonparametric methods under varying data dependence structures

author: Philippe Vieu
text: This paper investigates nonparametric regression estimation techniques for functional stationary ergodic data characterized by missing at random MAR mechanisms We address the challenges posed by the inherent dependencies and stochastic properties of functional data while simultaneously accommodating the missingness which complicates standard estimation methodologies Our approach combines advanced nonparametric regression methods with ergodic theory to develop robust estimators that remain consistent under MAR conditions We establish asymptotic properties of the proposed estimators demonstrating their convergence and efficiency in representing the underlying functional relationships Through extensive simulation studies and real data applications we highlight the performance of our methodology compared to traditional imputation and parametric regression techniques Our findings suggest that the proposed nonparametric approach not only mitigates biases introduced by missing data but also maintains the integrity of functional relationships in stationary ergodic settings This work contributes to the growing field of functional data analysis by providing a rigorous framework for handling missing observations in complex dependent data structures

author: Philippe Vieu
text: In this paper we develop a nonparametric estimation technique for surrogate density functions within the framework of infinitedimensional spaces Traditional density estimation methods often falter when applied to highdimensional data due to the curse of dimensionality and inherent complexities in functional relationships We propose a novel approach that leverages advanced kernel methods and regularization techniques to construct an estimator that is both computationally efficient and statistically robust Our method is grounded in the concept of reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces RKHS allowing us to capture the underlying structure of complex data distributions We establish asymptotic properties of the estimator demonstrating consistency and convergence rates under mild regularity conditions Additionally we provide simulations and case studies showcasing the applicability of our method in various fields including biostatistics and environmental modeling Our findings contribute to the growing body of research on nonparametric methods in highdimensional analysis offering practitioners a versatile tool for density estimation in challenging infinitedimensional settings

author: Philippe Vieu
text: AbstractThis paper investigates estimation and hypothesis testing in the context of partial linear regression models subjected to longmemory dependence Traditional regression techniques often assume independence or shortmemory properties of residuals which can lead to inefficient estimates and misleading inferences when these assumptions are violated We begin by introducing a framework for partial linear regression that accommodates longmemory processes allowing for flexible modeling of nonlinear relationships in the presence of persistent dependence Utilizing advanced asymptotic theory we derive the properties of least squares estimators and propose a generalized testing procedure for the significance of the linear components Simulation studies demonstrate the robustness of our proposed methodologies under various longmemory scenarios Finally we apply our model to a realworld dataset illustrating its practical utility and effectiveness in capturing the dynamics of complex relationships Our findings highlight the necessity of considering longmemory effects in econometric modeling and provide a solid foundation for future research in this direction

author: Philippe Vieu
text: We study regression estimation when the explanatory variable is functional Nonparametric estimates of the regression operator have been recently introduced They depend on a smoothing factor which controls its behavior and the aim of our work is to construct some datadriven criterion for choosing this smoothing parameter The criterion can be formulated in terms of a functional version of crossvalidation ideas Under mild assumptions on the unknown regression operator it is seen that this rule is asymptotically optimal As byproducts of this result we state some asymptotic equivalences for several measures of accuracy for nonparametric estimate of the regression operator We also present general inequalities for bounding moments of random sums involving functional variables Finally a short simulation study is carried out to illustrate the behavior of our method for finite samples c Elsevier BV

author: Philippe Vieu
text: We study the nonparametric regression estimation when the explanatory variable takes values in some functional space We establish some asymptotic results and we give the pointwise and uniform convergence of the kernel type estimator constructed from functional data under long memory conditions C Elsevier BV

author: Philippe Vieu
text: A method able to detect a possible common structure between two or more than two groups of curves is considered This technique is part of the recent developments within the field of Functional Data Analysis It is discussed how the standard approach based on factorial analysis for comparing groups of multivariate data can be used in this infinitedimensional framework The potentiality of such a functional method in terms of application is illustrated through a spectrometric functional data set coming from food industry quality control c Elsevier BV

author: Philippe Vieu
text: Kernel estimators of a regression function are investigated The bandwidths are locally chosen by a datadriven method based on the minimization of a local crossvalidation criterion This method is shown to be asymptotically optimal with respect to local quadratic measures of errors Monte Carlo experiments are presented and finally the method is applied to some data of medical interest

text: Recent advances in nonparametric functional data analysis allow to define the notion of mode for a sample of curves A kerneltype estimator is proposed for estimating this modal curve In addition other centrality curves can be easily extended to the functional case namely mean and median curves A nonparametric unsupervised classification method which is also a cluster analysis is investigated This is based on the comparison between the modal curve with another centrality curve for measuring some heterogeneity index The main point is to show the good practical behaviour of this hierarchical classification on a sample of radar waveforms registered from the satellite TopexPoscidon upon the Amazonian basin In addition a few theoretical advances are provided c Elsevier BV

author: Philippe Vieu
text: We suggest a way of reducing the very high dimension of a functional predictor X to a low number of dimensions chosen so as to give the best predictive performance Specifically if X is observed on a fine grid of design points t tr we propose a method for choosing a small subset of these say ti tik to optimize the prediction of a response variable Y The values tij are referred to as the most predictive design points or covariates for a given value of k and are computed using information contained in a set of independent observations Xi Yi of X Y The algorithm is based on local linear regression and calculations can be accelerated using linear regression to preselect the design points Boosting can be employed to further improve the predictive performance We illustrate the usefulness of our ideas through simulations and examples drawn from chemometrics and we develop theoretical arguments showing that the methodology can be applied successfully in a range of settings

author: Philippe Vieu
text: In the realm of functional data analysis nonparametric regression serves as a powerful tool for modeling complex relationships where traditional parametric frameworks may falter This paper presents a novel approach to automatic smoothing parameter selection in nonparametric regression for functional data We propose a hybrid algorithm that leverages crossvalidation and information criteria ensuring adaptability to diverse datasets with varying degrees of smoothness Our methodology systematically balances the biasvariance tradeoff optimizing the smoothing parameters without prior user intervention We extend our framework to accommodate highdimensional functional data and demonstrate its effectiveness through extensive simulation studies and realworld applications in fields such as finance and environmental science The results indicate significant improvements in estimation accuracy and predictive performance over existing methods This work not only enhances the toolkit for functional data analysis but also paves the way for more robust and automated analytical pipelines in applied statistics The proposed approach is implemented in an accessible software package facilitating its adoption by practitioners

author: Philippe Vieu
text: This paper investigates the consistency of regression estimators when applied to functional data under long memory conditions Functional data analysis FDA has gained prominence in various fields due to its ability to handle complex highdimensional datasets characterized by curves surfaces or more generally functions However the presence of long memory properties which imply persistent correlations across observations poses significant challenges to the standard regression frameworks traditionally employed in FDA We formally define the long memory processes in the context of functional data and propose a class of regression estimators tailored to accommodate such dependencies Through a series of theoretical derivations we establish sufficient conditions for the consistency of these estimators utilizing tools from both functional analysis and long memory theory Our findings are supported by extensive simulation studies that illustrate the performance of the proposed estimators relative to existing methods in various long memory scenarios Finally we apply our methodology to a realworld dataset demonstrating the practical implications of our theoretical results This work not only advances the understanding of regression techniques in the presence of long memory but also contributes to the growing field of functional data analysis by providing robust solutions to complex data structures

author: Philippe Vieu
text: In the field of statistical analysis understanding and comparing the dynamics of groups characterized by curves is essential for drawing meaningful conclusions This paper presents a novel factorbased method for comparing groups of curves allowing for a comprehensive examination of their underlying structures and variations We introduce a framework that integrates factor analysis with advanced curve fitting techniques to identify significant factors that contribute to the variation among groups The methodology is rigorously applied to both simulated datasets and realworld applications demonstrating its robustness and versatility Our results reveal distinct patterns and shared characteristics among the groups highlighting the potential for this approach in exploratory data analysis and hypothesis testing By providing a systematic way to compare complex curve shapes this study contributes to the existing literature on multivariate analysis and offers practitioners a valuable tool for interpreting curveassociated data across various domains

author: Philippe Vieu
text: Nonparametric regression techniques have gained traction for their flexibility in modeling complex relationships between variables without imposing rigid structural assumptions A critical aspect of nonparametric regression is the selection of the bandwidth which governs the level of smoothness in the estimated function In this paper we propose a novel approach for optimal local bandwidth selection in nonparametric regression using a crossvalidation framework coupled with a biasvariance tradeoff analysis We explore the implications of various bandwidth selection methods including plugin estimators and datadriven approaches and we assess their performance through extensive simulation studies Our findings reveal that the proposed method significantly enhances prediction accuracy and reduces estimation error compared to traditional bandwidth selection techniques We illustrate the effectiveness of our approach with realworld data applications demonstrating its robustness in capturing underlying patterns in diverse datasets The results underscore the importance of optimal local bandwidth choice in refining nonparametric regression models thereby contributing to more reliable and interpretable statistical analyses

author: Philippe Vieu
text: In this paper we investigate the efficacy of modal curves as a tool for the classification of radar waveforms Radar systems generate a wide variety of waveforms each possessing distinct characteristics that are crucial for accurate target detection and identification Traditional classification methods often struggle with complexity and variability in waveforms leading to suboptimal performance We propose a novel approach that leverages modal curves representations derived from statistical modal analysis to encapsulate the intrinsic features of radar waveforms By employing modal curve analysis we enhance waveform representation and enable more robust classification across diverse scenarios Our methodology involves extracting modal curves from a comprehensive dataset of radar signals followed by the application of machine learning algorithms to classify these waveforms based on their modal characteristics We present empirical results demonstrating significant improvements in classification accuracy compared to existing techniques This work highlights the potential of modal curves as a powerful tool for advancing the field of radar signal processing offering insights into the underlying statistical structures of radar waveforms that enhance classification performance in complex environments

author: Philippe Vieu
text: AbstractIn the realm of functional data analysis the selection of design points plays a crucial role in enhancing predictive accuracy and model interpretability This paper introduces a novel methodology for identifying mostpredictive design points for functional data predictors focusing on maximizing the efficiency of predictive models in complex data environments We develop a statistical framework that incorporates both the inherent structure of functional data and the underlying relationships between predictors and responses Utilizing a combination of optimal design theory and machine learning techniques our approach systematically evaluates candidate design points based on their predictive utility across a diverse set of scenarios Through extensive simulations and realdata applications we illustrate the effectiveness of our proposed method in improving predictive performance compared to traditional design selection strategies Our findings underscore the importance of strategic design point selection in functional data contexts providing a robust tool for researchers and practitioners seeking to refine their predictive models The implications for future research and potential applications in various fields including biostatistics environmental modeling and economics are also discussed

text: In bivariate density representation there is an extensive literature on level set estimation when the level is fixed but this is not so much the case when choosing which level is or which levels are of most interest This is an important practical question which depends on the kind of problem one has to deal with as well as the kind of feature one wishes to highlight in the density the answer to which requires both the definition of what the optimal level is and the construction of a method for finding it We consider two scenarios for this problem The first one corresponds to situations in which one has just a single density function to be represented However as a result of the technical progress in data collecting problems are emerging in which one has to deal with a sample of densities In these situations the need arises to develop joint representation for all these densities and this is the second scenario considered in this paper For each case we provide consistency results for the estimated levels and present wide Monte Carlo simulated experiments illustrating the interest and feasibility of the proposed method C Elsevier Inc

author: Philippe Vieu
text: We consider kernel regression estimate when both the response variable and the explanatory one are functional The rates of uniform almost complete convergence are stated as function of the small ball probability of the predictor and as function of the entropy of the set on which uniformity is obtained

author: Philippe Vieu
text: The bandwidth selection problem in kernel density estimation is investigated in situations where the observed data are dependent The classical leaveout technique is extended and thereby a class of crossvalidated bandwidths is defined These bandwidths are shown to be asymptotically optimal under a strong mixing condition The leaveone out or ordinary form of crossvalidation remains asymptotically optimal under the dependence model considered However a simulation study shows that when the data are strongly enough correlated the ordinary version of crossvalidation can be improved upon in finitesized samples

author: Philippe Vieu
text: A new nonparametric tool for studying the relationship between a curve considered as a functional predictor and a categorical response is proposed This is typically a problem of discrimination also known as supervised classification but applied to a sample of curves Starting from a food industry context and a speech recognition problem we nonparametrically estimate the posterior probability that an incoming curve is of a given class A consistent kernel estimator is introduced and its practical performance is pointed out by means of a simulation study Finally this method is applied to the abovementioned data sets C Elsevier BV

author: Philippe Vieu
text: We develop a nonparametric test based on kernel smoothers in order to decide whether some covariates could be suppressed in a multidimensional nonparametric regression study We give the asymptotic distribution of the statistic involved in our test under a general dependence assumption on the sample that allows for application to time series prediction C Elsevier Science BV

author: Philippe Vieu
text: AbstractIn this paper we explore a novel approach to regression analysis where both the response variable and predictors are treated as functions rather than traditional scalar values This functional regression framework allows for capturing complex relationships that may be missed in classical approaches particularly in scenarios involving longitudinal data curves or spatial processes We develop a comprehensive theoretical foundation for functional regression including estimation methods hypothesis testing and model selection criteria Furthermore we present a simulation study to illustrate the effectiveness of our proposed methods comparing them with standard regression techniques We apply our approach to realworld datasets from various fields demonstrating its capability to uncover intricate functional dependencies Finally we discuss potential extensions of our methods and their implications for advancing functional data analysis Our findings highlight the importance of considering a functional perspective in regression settings paving the way for more robust and insightful statistical modeling

author: Philippe Vieu
text: In this paper we investigate the efficacy of modal curves as a tool for the classification of radar waveforms Radar systems generate a wide variety of waveforms each possessing distinct characteristics that are crucial for accurate target detection and identification Traditional classification methods often struggle with complexity and variability in waveforms leading to suboptimal performance We propose a novel approach that leverages modal curves representations derived from statistical modal analysis to encapsulate the intrinsic features of radar waveforms By employing modal curve analysis we enhance waveform representation and enable more robust classification across diverse scenarios Our methodology involves extracting modal curves from a comprehensive dataset of radar signals followed by the application of machine learning algorithms to classify these waveforms based on their modal characteristics We present empirical results demonstrating significant improvements in classification accuracy compared to existing techniques This work highlights the potential of modal curves as a powerful tool for advancing the field of radar signal processing offering insights into the underlying statistical structures of radar waveforms that enhance classification performance in complex environments

author: Philippe Vieu
text: In this paper we explore nonparametric regression techniques applied to functional data focusing on both statistical inference and practical implementation Functional data which encompasses observations that are curves images or other infinitedimensional objects presents unique challenges for traditional regression methodologies We propose a comprehensive framework that integrates multiple nonparametric approaches to regression analysis including kernel smoothing and spline methods tailored for the complexities of functional data structures We establish the theoretical underpinnings of our techniques demonstrating convergence rates and asymptotic properties under various conditions Through extensive simulations we assess the finitesample performance of our methods identifying scenarios where nonparametric approaches outperform parametric counterparts We further discuss practical considerations such as bandwidth selection and computational efficiency providing a userfriendly guide for practitioners in various fields including biostatistics econometrics and environmental sciences Our results underscore the versatility and robustness of nonparametric regression in handling diverse types of functional data paving the way for more accurate modeling and inference in realworld applications We conclude with case studies that illustrate the practical utility of our methodologies highlighting their implications for future research and exploratory data analysis in functional contexts

author: Philippe Vieu
text: This paper addresses the challenge of optimal representation of bivariate probability densities through level sets a crucial aspect in statistical analysis and data visualization We introduce a systematic approach to determine optimal level sets that minimize the discrepancy between the true density function and its estimated representation while ensuring computational efficiency By leveraging techniques from multivariate analysis and information theory we develop a framework that identifies the most informative contours of the bivariate distribution Our proposed method integrates both analytical and numerical strategies providing a robust procedure for constructing level sets that enhance interpretability and facilitate statistical inference We showcase the effectiveness of our approach through simulation studies and realworld applications demonstrating significant improvements in representation quality compared to traditional methods The implications of our findings extend to various fields including machine learning spatial statistics and econometrics where understanding complex relationships within bivariate data is essential

author: Philippe Vieu
text: In this paper we explore kernel regression techniques tailored for functional responses expanding traditional regression methodologies to accommodate scenarios where the dependent variable manifests as a function rather than a scalar The proposed approach leverages kernel smoothing to estimate the relationship between a multivariate covariate and a functional response facilitating more nuanced modeling of data in areas such as finance medicine and environmental science where responses are often curves or surfaces We introduce a novel kernelbased estimator for functional regression establish its theoretical properties and demonstrate its consistency and asymptotic normality under weak dependence assumptions Empirical performance is evaluated through simulations and case studies illustrating the methods robustness in capturing complex relationships compared to existing approaches The findings indicate that our functional kernel regression framework provides a powerful tool for analyzing the intricacies inherent in functional data opening avenues for future research in both methodology and application

author: Philippe Vieu
text: AbstractThis paper presents a robust methodology for selecting optimal bandwidth in kernel density estimation KDE when dealing with dependent data structures Traditional approaches to bandwidth selection primarily cater to independent and identically distributed iid samples where the assumptions underlying conventional techniques may not hold Our proposed datadriven algorithm adapts to the complexities introduced by dependence utilizing advanced statistical tools to accurately capture the underlying data distribution We employ a combination of theoretical analysis and empirical simulations to assess the performance of our bandwidth selection criterion across various dependency models including autoregressive processes and moving average structures The effectiveness of our approach is demonstrated through a series of applications in realworld datasets revealing improved density estimates compared to standard methods Additionally we discuss the implications of our findings for fields such as econometrics environmental statistics and bioinformatics where data dependencies are prevalent This work contributes to the literature by providing a practical solution for bandwidth selection in the context of dependent data enhancing the reliability of density estimation practices in applied statistics Keywords Kernel Density Estimation Bandwidth Selection Dependent Data Statistical Methods DataDriven Approaches

author: Philippe Vieu
text: In this paper we introduce a novel nonparametric functional approach for the discrimination of curves focusing on the analysis of complex data where traditional parametric techniques may fall short We propose a framework that effectively captures the underlying patterns in functional data through the application of advanced metrics and techniques such as Dynamic Time Warping and Functional Principal Component Analysis Our approach emphasizes the flexibility of nonparametric methods allowing for the identification of significant features and variations across curves without imposing strict parametric forms We validate the proposed methodology through extensive simulations and realworld applications demonstrating its superior performance in discriminating between curves compared to existing parametric counterparts The results indicate potentially transformative implications for fields such as medical imaging biology and finance where curve analysis plays a critical role Our findings provide a comprehensive toolkit for researchers seeking to leverage nonparametric techniques in the realm of functional data analysis paving the way for future explorations in curve discrimination and beyond

author: Philippe Vieu
text: Abstract Variable selection is a crucial aspect of nonparametric regression particularly when dealing with dependent data that exhibit complex structures This paper presents a comprehensive exploration of variable selection techniques tailored for nonparametric regression models in the presence of dependence among observations We investigate the limitations of traditional variable selection methods in this context and propose a novel framework that integrates dependency structures into the selection process Utilizing a combination of resampling techniques and penalization approaches we demonstrate how our method enhances model interpretability and predictive performance Through simulation studies and realworld applications we illustrate the efficacy of our proposed techniques highlighting their ability to properly identify relevant predictors while accounting for dependence This note contributes to the ongoing discourse on nonparametric regression by providing practical insights and methodological advancements for researchers and practitioners confronting the challenges posed by dependent data

author: Philippe Vieu
text: It is wellknown that pure nonparametric techniques perform less and less well when the dimension of the regression function increases because of the sparsness of the data We attack this curse of dimensionality by proposing a method to select a set of regressors Optimality with respect to quadratic loss function is shown Then simulated examples are presented to illustrate both curse of dimensionality and behaviour of the variables selection procedure

author: Philippe Vieu
text: This note investigates the consistency properties of the kerneltype estimator of a quantile in the setting of a long memory stationary stochastic process Under a general longrange dependence situation without any restriction of gaussian type we give consistency results and rates of convergence An interesting byproduct of this paper is a new consistency result for kerneltype estimator of a smooth distribution function with rates over the whole real line C Elsevier BV

author: Philippe Vieu
text: This paper focuses on partially linear regression models with several real and functional covariates The aim is to construct an estimate of the variance of the error In our model a realvalued response variable is explained by the sum of an unknown linear combination of the components of a multivariate random variable and an unknown transformation of a functional random variable and the second sample moment based on residuals from a semiparametric fit is proposed for estimating the error variance Then the asymptotic normality and the law of the iterated logarithm of such estimator are obtained Finally a simulation study illustrates the finite sample behaviour of the estimator while an application to real data shows the usefulness of the proposed methodology more specifically for confidence region construction

author: Philippe Vieu
text: Additive model and estimates for regression problems involving functional data are proposed The impact of the additive methodology for analyzing datasets involving various functional covariates is underlined by comparing its predictive power with those of standard ie non additive nonparametric functional regression methods The comparison is made both from a theoretical point of view and from a real environmental functional dataset As a byproduct the method is also used for boosting nonparametric functional data analysis even in situations where a single functional covariate is observed A second functional dataset coming from spectrometric analysis illustrates the interest of this functional boosting procedure C Elsevier BV

author: Philippe Vieu
text: The general framework of this paper deals with the nonparametric regression of a scalar response on a functional variable ie one observation can be a curve surface or any other object lying into an infinitedimensional space This paper proposes to model local behaviour of the regression operator ie the link between a scalar response and an explanatory functional variable To this end one introduces a functional approach in the same spirit as local linear ideas in nonparametric regression The main advantage of this functional local method is to propose an explicit expression of a kerneltype estimator which makes its computation easy and fast while keeping good predictive performance Asymptotic properties are stated and a functional data set illustrates the good behaviour of this functional locally modelled regression method

author: Philippe Vieu
text: This paper is on regression models when the explanatory variable is a function The question is to look for which among the pn discretized values of the function must be incorporated in the model The aim of the paper is to show how the continuous structure of the data allows to develop new specific variable selection procedures which improve the rates of convergence of the estimated parameters and need much less restrictive assumptions on pn C Elsevier BV

author: Philippe Vieu
text: The choice of regressors in nonparametric estimation is a critical factor that influences the efficiency accuracy and interpretability of predictive models This paper investigates various strategies for selecting appropriate regressors in nonparametric settings focusing on kernel regression and spline smoothing techniques We begin by reviewing existing literature on regressor selection highlighting the challenges posed by highdimensional data and the potential for overfitting We propose a systematic framework for regressor selection that incorporates datadriven methodologies such as crossvalidation and stability selection Additionally we introduce a novel algorithm that utilizes feature relevance metrics to prioritize regressors while maintaining flexibility in model complexity Through extensive simulation studies and realworld applications we demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed methods in improving estimation accuracy while controlling for bias and variance Our findings provide valuable insights for practitioners and researchers seeking to enhance nonparametric models through informed regressor selection contributing to more robust analyses in fields such as economics biostatistics and machine learning

author: Philippe Vieu
text: This paper addresses the challenges of quantile estimation in the context of longrange dependent LRD stochastic processes where traditional methods may yield biased or inconsistent results due to the intricate dependence structures inherent in such processes We provide a comprehensive analysis of existing quantile estimation techniques and their limitations when applied to LRD processes Building on foundational results from the theory of longrange dependence we propose a novel estimation methodology that incorporates the fractional order of integration and utilizes appropriate scaling limits Our approach is validated through Monte Carlo simulations which demonstrate improved accuracy and robustness compared to conventional estimators Furthermore we illustrate the practical applicability of our method through case studies involving financial time series data characterized by LRD properties The paper contributes to the ongoing discourse on robust statistical inference under longrange dependence and offers a pathway for more reliable quantile estimates in fields where modeling such complexities is crucial

author: Philippe Vieu
text: Abstract Variable selection is a crucial aspect of nonparametric regression particularly when dealing with dependent data that exhibit complex structures This paper presents a comprehensive exploration of variable selection techniques tailored for nonparametric regression models in the presence of dependence among observations We investigate the limitations of traditional variable selection methods in this context and propose a novel framework that integrates dependency structures into the selection process Utilizing a combination of resampling techniques and penalization approaches we demonstrate how our method enhances model interpretability and predictive performance Through simulation studies and realworld applications we illustrate the efficacy of our proposed techniques highlighting their ability to properly identify relevant predictors while accounting for dependence This note contributes to the ongoing discourse on nonparametric regression by providing practical insights and methodological advancements for researchers and practitioners confronting the challenges posed by dependent data

author: Philippe Vieu
text: This paper addresses the challenge of error variance estimation in semifunctional partially linear regression models which are increasingly utilized in econometrics and social sciences for their ability to model complex relationships involving both functional and nonfunctional predictors We develop a novel estimation technique that combines robust statistical methods and asymptotic theory to provide accurate estimates of error variance in these models Our method accounts for the inherent structure of functional data while managing the nonparametric components effectively Through extensive simulation studies we demonstrate that our approach outperforms existing methods in terms of bias variance and overall mean squared error especially under varying degrees of functional complexity and sample sizes Additionally we apply our proposed method to a realworld dataset illustrating its practical applicability and the importance of accurate error variance estimation in enhancing model interpretation and inference The findings contribute valuable insights toward improving the reliability of statistical inference in semifunctional partially linear regression frameworks paving the way for future research in this area

author: Philippe Vieu
text: In this paper we introduce a novel framework for modeling functional data through additive prediction and boosting techniques Functional data characterized by continuous trajectories or curves poses unique challenges for traditional statistical methodologies We propose an additive model that captures the intrinsic structure of functional data by decomposing it into sum components facilitating interpretation and effective prediction Building upon this foundation we incorporate boosting algorithms to enhance predictive performance leveraging the strengths of ensemble learning to sequentially refine the model Through extensive simulations and realworld applications we demonstrate the efficacy of our approach in improving prediction accuracy and reducing bias particularly in highdimensional settings Our findings suggest that additive prediction coupled with boosting provides a robust strategy for analyzing functional data offering significant advantages over existing methodologies This work contributes to the growing field of functional data analysis and opens avenues for further research into advanced statistical techniques tailored to complex highdimensional data structures

author: Philippe Vieu
text: In the realm of statistical analysis the integration of locally modelled regression techniques with functional data has garnered increasing attention due to its potential to enhance modeling flexibility and interpretability This paper presents a comprehensive framework for locally modelled regression specifically tailored for functional data contexts where observations are represented as curves or surfaces rather than traditional scalar values We develop a novel approach that incorporates local fitting procedures to capture the nuanced variations in functional datasets facilitating the identification of intricate patterns and relationship dynamics Through rigorous theoretical foundations we derive consistency and convergence properties for our proposed estimators ensuring robustness in various statistical settings The efficacy of our methodology is demonstrated through extensive simulations and realdata applications highlighting its advantages in terms of predictive accuracy and interpretability compared to conventional global regression methods We discuss the implications of our findings for practitioners in fields such as medicine finance and environmental science where functional data are prevalent By bridging locally modelled regression with functional analysis this work aims to expand the toolkit available for data scientists facing the complexities of highdimensional structured data

author: Philippe Vieu
text: In the realm of statistical modeling variable selection remains a paramount challenge particularly in infinitedimensional settings such as functional data analysis highdimensional regression and nonparametric modeling This paper introduces a novel framework for variable selection in infinitedimensional problems leveraging recent advancements in statistics and machine learning By employing penalization techniques and adaptive algorithms we propose a methodology that effectively identifies influential variables while maintaining computational efficiency Our approach extends classical variable selection methods incorporating regularization strategies that accommodate the intricacies of infinitedimensional spaces The theoretical foundations are laid out demonstrating consistency and asymptotic properties of the proposed methods We illustrate the practical applicability of our framework through simulation studies and real data examples showing significant improvements in model interpretability and predictive performance Our findings contribute to a deeper understanding of variable selection in complex statistical models and offer valuable insights for practitioners operating in highdimensional and infinitedimensional contexts
